items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Louie disputed me about him and them and having a bucket contest on the boat.

ctx.x: Now here's another thing. When he died, Bill, this is the God's truth, so help me. So help me. When he died, there was two things that his mother had. And if I'd only got them, you see, Louie disputed me about him and them and having a bucket contest on the boat.

by the name of Jack Pettis, and we used to run across Louis every once in a while, you know. Let's take one more break here, and then we'll come back and listen to some more from that album, and also some old Duke Ellington that's kind of interesting. We'll be back on jazz review after this word. Now, a few words about the Sony 250A tape deck. Forget it. Forget about leaving it on. much about the Ellington band at the Cotton Club? Yeah, I used to go up there quite a bit because at that time everything was in Harlem. You know, there wasn't anything. They had big clubs downtown, but there was no jazz downtown in New York at all, and everything was in Harlem. And Jack Teegarden was playing with Benny Pollock. And they worked at the hotel and used to get off at one o'clock, so Jack and I would run up and get ahead of a bunch of these underground places, Budbee's and Susie's and all the way…
